newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rice, cereals management committee meets.
newsitem.headline: EU rice, cereals management committee meets.

text.p: European Union cereals and rice management committee will set refunds for processed products and starch at a two-day meeting starting on Thursday, an EU official said on Wednesday.
"The cereals and rice management committee will fix processed product refunds for products in Annex II, non-Annex II and compound feed," the official said.
The committee is also scheduled to fix refunds for starch.
Retrospective refunds of import duty paid on imports of Norwegian fish meal feed are expected to be scaled back .
"The European Commission has received applications relating to shipments which amount to double the annual quota," the official said.
The Commission invited applications for retrospective repayment of duty because the regulation introducing the duty- free quota was published late in the EU Official Journal last year.
There will also be a vote on a proposal allowing Austrian pet food importers to reclaim duty.
"The Austrian government was unaware of a duty free quota allowance for imports of dog and cat food from Hungary last year and this will allow them to make repayments," the official said.
Refunds for shipments of rice and cereals to the Canaries and Poseidom countries will be set.
A regulation introducing area aid for rice producers will be voted on and is expected to be approved.
"The item has been postponed a number of times but is listed for a vote this week," the official said.
Area aid payments are being introduced to compensate EU producers for cuts in intervention prices under the reform of the rice regime.
The committee will vote on the renewal of the 1995 Polish starch agreement.
"The annual quota arrangement allowing duty free imports of up to 7,000 tonnes of starch from Poland (Reg: 3066/95) runs out at the end of this year and needs to be renewed," the official said.
